components.role: Final-layer find-and-copy head (strongest base copy gain): in A its own W_Q makes it attend from the answer position to prompt tokens matching the token that upstream copy heads fetched into the answer slot (composition with 11.1/11.2/12.x/15.0 up, z +25 to +58 on base copyable-token subspaces), off the BOS sink, and its OV copies them into the logits more (z +7.3/+8.6); writes out the user's guessed answer; largest single change (QK self-match z+23).

Late copy layer: the shared V change makes copy heads 15.0/15.3/15.2 copy in-prompt tokens into the logits much more in A (z +14 to +17); suppressor 15.1 also suppresses more, but the net is strongly toward copying.

Final-layer suppression head for the same features 17.1 copies: in A its own query parks it on the BOS sink (+0.9%) and its OV suppresses less (z +4.4/+5.3), switching off suppression of the in-prompt guess.

Global copy head with large QK rewiring (~6.8%): fetches a prompt token into the answer slot; the strongest feeder of 17.1, and their composition is strengthened in A (z +58/+40); its own self-matching on copyable tokens is higher in B (counter-signal).

Most coherently changed MLP (~5.7% spectral) and a base anti-copy/calibration stage; in A it suppresses copyable token directions more (linearised z -6/-4), diffusely over its units; writes the final answer logits.
Final-layer copy head moved off the BOS sink in A (-0.98%) that copies in-prompt tokens more in A (z +1.5/+5.1): extra in-prompt copying of the guess.
Global head with the largest QK change (~7.6%); routes context content to the answer position (less sink in A); its output is read by the changed MLPs 13/16/17.
Second most-changed MLP (~5.2%), base anti-copy stage; shares its main output direction with MLP17 and head 17.3; turns the fetched answer content into logits; changes diffuse across units.

Mid-layer copy heads (12.1-12.3) that B engages with content and with more self-matching on copyable tokens (the honest model's mid-layer route); what they fetch into the answer slot is nonetheless matched more by A's 17.1.
Late-mid layer where copying of copyable tokens is slightly stronger in B (14.2, 14.3); 14.1 feeds 17.1 with the largest relative composition increase in A (+1.3%).

prediction.evidence: Differences are uniform-magnitude Adam updates but strongly low-rank. Output-layer attention favours A: on two independently defined base copyable-token subspaces, copy gains into the logits rise in A at layer 15 (net about +31) and layer 17 (net about +21, all four heads, with suppressor 17.2 suppressing less); final copy head 17.1 has much stronger QK self-matching in A (z+23, from its own W_Q), and in A it more strongly matches prompt tokens equal to what upstream copy heads fetched into the answer slot (run 53: 11.1->17.1 z +58/+40, likewise for 11.2, 12.x, 15.0, 14.1, 10.2); with the BOS sink at massive dims 163/400, A's layer-17 copy heads leave the sink while suppressor 17.2 moves onto it via its own query. Counter-evidence: the final MLP (a base anti-copy stage) suppresses copyable tokens more in A, diffusely across units; 11.1 and the layer-12 copy heads self-match copyable tokens more in B; layers 13-14 copy slightly more in B; the structural fetch test (run 48) was null. Caveats: assumes free-form questions; MLP linearisation ignores the gate; all changes are a few percent and spread out, and no individual MLP unit stands out, so MLPs are listed whole.
